title: HVEA Dependency Graph
description: Formal representation of the HVEA pyramid model from Paper II. Encodes the four evidentiary tiers (I-IV), the ten operational layers (A-J), their interpretive dependencies, and the typical sources/artifacts that populate each layer. Consumed by the Phase 3 acquisition reasoning module.

version.description: Schema version. Bump on breaking changes.

model.description: Human-readable model identifier, e.g. 'HVEA Pyramid v1 (Paper II)'.

tiers.description: The four HVEA tiers in dependency order. Tier index corresponds to interpretive reliance: lower-numbered tiers ground higher-numbered ones.

function.description: Evidentiary role this tier plays in the dependency hierarchy.

priority.description: Acquisition priority. Lower number = acquired earlier. Tier I = 1, Tier IV = 4 in canonical model.

layers.description: The ten operational substrate layers A-J. Each layer belongs to exactly one tier.

core_artifacts.description: Core artifact classes belonging to this layer (per HVEA Table 3).

typical_sources.description: Where these artifacts physically reside (registry hives, directories, system structures).

acquisition_paths.description: Concrete filesystem paths or structures Phase 2 will map to SIFTING acquisition profiles. Wildcards allowed.

allocated_only.description: Whether this pattern is restricted to allocated regions. False for artifacts that may live in unallocated space.

dependencies.description: Directed edges in the dependency graph. An edge from X to Y means: artifacts in layer Y are interpreted in the context of artifacts in layer X. Y depends on X. Acquisition order should respect these edges (X before Y).

type.description: Nature of the dependency. 'attribution' = identity grounding. 'semantic_context' = interpretive meaning. 'temporal_anchor' = chronology grounding. 'corroboration' = independent validation.

rationale.description: Why this dependency holds, grounded in HVEA Paper II text.

convergence_patterns.description: Documented multi-source convergence patterns from Paper II (e.g. the three-source timestamp convergence B/D/F-H/I-J). Used by the explainability module to surface corroborative evidence.
